outcome: serial anthropometric measures (z-scores of INTERGROWTH-21st preterm postnatal growth standards)
cohort: The study included 2320 singleton and 1180 twin preterm newborns across very, moderate, and late preterm categories, monitored until hospital discharge.
finding: Etiologically-based preterm sub-groups ('perinatal sepsis', 'suspected IUGR', and 'fetal distress') among very and late preterm infants exhibited lower postnatal growth patterns compared to the 'no main condition' reference sub-group, with this pattern persisting in late but not very preterm infants after correcting for birth weight z-score.
followup_time: Up to hospital discharge, with the last anthropometric measure taken at a median postmenstrual age of 37 weeks.
gest_age: Preterm newborns, including very preterm (<28 weeks' gestation), moderate preterm, and late preterm categories.
